Chest, abdomen, leg, and back pain; diarrhea and constipation
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with h/o possible mast cell 
degranulation syndrome who presented to the emergency room with 
complaint of chest pain and abdominal pain typical of her 
mastocytosis flares.  
.  
The patient has numerous complaints, including burning 
epigastric pain, ""whole leg"" pain and spasms, diarrhea, and 
abdominal pain. She believes this symptoms are from a flare of 
her mastocytosis, which she thinks was triggered by a UTI. She 
was given levofloxacin from ___, but was unable to 
fill the Rx because of the cost. She then contacted her PCP, who 
started her on cipro, of which she has had 2 doses. She is 
concerned because she is having b/l lower abdominal pain and leg 
spasms, which are not typical for her mast cell degranulation 
flares.  
.  
In the ED, initial VS were: 97.0 ___ 22 99%. During her 
stay in the ED, she remained tachycardic with stable pressures. 
Nursing notes document that she was restless and tearful in her 
bed. Exam was notable for lower abdominal tenderness. Labs were 
remarkable for positive UA. CT abd/pelvis was obtained because 
of complaint of RLQ pain; according to prelim read, there was no 
acute process. She was given dilaudid IV, ativan, and benadryl 
IV according to her protocol. She also received phenazopyridine 
100mg PO, ciprofloxacin, and 2L of IV fluids.  
.  
Upon arrival to the floor, she was most concerned about her leg 
and thigh pain.  
.  
On review of systems, she endorses low grade fevers to 100.4 at 
home. In the ED, she had complained of shortness of breath and 
cough.

___ CXR

as seen on both

of ___ no diagnostic interim change. 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
  
___ F with numerous admissions to ___ for symptoms attributed 
to reported Mast Cell Degranulation syndrome that is being 
called into question per recent notes, presents with multitude 
of complaints including chest pain, abdominal pain, back pain, 
leg pain, diarrhea, constipation, headaches, low grade 
fevers--similar in nature to previous admissions within the past 
2 weeks, also now with UTI. 

1. Mast Cell Degranulation/Activation syndrome--The diagnosis of 
Mast Cell Activation was made based on an elevated 24hr urine 
histamine elevation at ___. During her past admission Dr. 
___ (___). The allergist thought 
that the patient does not have systemic mastocytosis based on a 
negative ___ Bx at ___ and multiple normal serum tryptase levels 
(please see OMR note ___, however this does not rule out 
that she has Mast Cell Degranulation/Activation syndrome. In 
addition it has to be taken into account that the communication 
between the patients allergist at the ___ and her inpatient 
providers and gastroenterologist at the ___ has been difficult 
and neither site has access to the entire diagnostic data on the 
patient.
The patient was treated per her prescribed protocol for flare 
including IV Dilaudid, Benadryl, and Ativan on admission. She 
was also continued on Cromolyn and Ranitidine. An allergy 
consult was called, who suggested that the pt may have some 
element of mast cell activation and helped facilitate her 
further care.
It was decided that because of the pt's fragmentation of care 
and the difficulties in communication that she would be best 
served by establishing care with another allergist at ___, Dr. 
___, with whom an appointment was made.
A component of the pt's clinical picture was also thought to be 
due to psychiatric illness, and the pt was offered Psychiatric 
consultation, however she declined. 

2. Positive urinalysis with h/o recurrent UTIs--The pt had 2 
doses of Cipro from her PCP and was continued on Ciprofloxacin 
on admission. She was discharged on Cipro to complete a 7 day 
course. However, the culture and sensitivities came back after 
the pt had been discharged, and was Ecoli resistant to Cipro. 
The pt was called on ___ and told to stop the Cipro 
and take Nitrofurantoin 100mg PO bid for 7 days to which the E 
coli was sensitive, after which she would continue her 
maintenance dose of 50mg PO daily for prophylaxis. When asked if 
she needed a prescription called in, she went to find her meds 
and stated that she had 100's and 50's and had at least 14 doses 
of the 100's, and that they had been filled just last month. She 
understood the instructions that were given to 
her--Nitrofurantoin 100mg PO bid x7d then restart maintenance 
50mg PO qday. 

3. Atypical white cells and eosinophilia--Was noted in previous 
admissions and thought to be part of the above mentioned 
syndrome. A Heme/Onc for possible repeat BM Bx, can be 
considered as an outpatient. 

4. Abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation--The pt received 
another abdomen/pelvis CT which did show any pathology to 
explain any symptoms. Pain was controlled per the above 
protocol. The pt was repeatedly seen to be sleeping comfortably 
and up around walking the halls without pain or difficulty, yet 
when asked complained of severe, constant abdominal pain. No 
peritoneal signs or acute abdomen was seen during this 
admission. Diarrhea and constipation were not an acute issue 
this admission. 

5. Lingula abnormality seen on CXR--Spoke with radiology about 
this who felt that the original CXR read was overcalled and the 
opacity was very slight and subtle. They stated that if 
clinically warranted a repeat PA and lateral could be done, but 
as pt was without WBC count, fevers, cough, or unexplainable 
pulmonary symptoms, this was deferred to be followed up on an 
outpt basis. 

6. Parodoxical Vocal Cord Dysfunction--Noted in pt's history, 
however this was not an active issue this admission. 
  
7. H/o Syncope--Patient has POE alert describing history of 
throwing herself on the floor, and also with positive tilt table 
results in her records. She was continued on home Midodrine, 
kept on fall precautions, and this was not an issue this 
admission. 

8. Anxiety/Depression--Pt was continued on home Doxepin and 
Duloxetine, and declined inpt Psychiatric evaluation. 

9. ADHD--Pt was continued on home Adderall. 

10. GERD--Pt was continued on home PPI and this was not an 
active issue this admission.  

11. Osteoarthritis--Pt was continued on home Plaquenil. 
  
12. Anemia--Pt with baseline Hct ___, and was within baseline 
this admission. Pt was continued on home Iron med.

Home
 
Discharge Diagnosis:
Primary: 
Atypical Chest Pain
Right Lower Quadrant Abdominal Pain
Inappropriate Mast Cell Activation
Urinary Tract Infection

 
Discharge Condition:
Stable.  Ambulating without assistance.  Breathing comfortably 
on room air. 

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were seen and evaluated for your chest pain.  It was felt 
that your symptoms were related to your mast cell degranulation 
syndrome.  You were also diagnosed with a urinary tract 
infection. 

Please take all your medications as prescribed.  The following 
changes were made to your medication regimen. 
1. Please take ciprofloxacin 500 mg two times a day for four 
more days
2. Please hold your nitrofurantoin until you complete your 
course of antibiotics for your urinary tract infection.  Then 
you should resume. 

Please keep all your followup appointments as scheduled.  

Please seek immediate medical attention if you experience any 
fevers, chills, worsening chest pain, difficulty breathing, or 
any other concerning symptoms.
